frequency_question: How often are multi-year bilateral technical resource treaties successfully negotiated, drafted, and signed from inception of formal successor talks to final execution within a sub-four-month final window?
membership_rule: Includes all bilateral water-sharing treaties involving major transboundary river basins undergoing formal expiration and successor renewal processes since 1950. Excludes unilateral declarations or non-binding administrative arrangements lacking treaty status.

cases.name: Treaty on sharing of Teesta water (Drafted but stalled)

coverage_note: 4 named major regional precedents identified; universe of comparable major transboundary water treaty renewals in South Asia is small and bounded.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sub-basin level administrative understandings that bypassed formal parliamentary or cabinet treaty ratification paths.
skeleton: Total recorded major South Asian transboundary water negotiations requiring joint technical committee reports (4 observed cases) where technical data compilation takes ~60 days, legal drafting takes ~30 days, and cabinet clearance takes ~20 days, totaling a minimum physical duration of 110 sequential calendar days without allowance for procedural recycling.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 attempted frameworks successfully completed within designated operational horizons.
validity_reason: Bilateral treaty-making procedures, bureaucratic drafting speeds, and cabinet approval structures in the region remain stable over decades, changing only via constitutional overhauls.
